items.headline: AI Spending Fears Hammer Big Tech Stocks
items.excerpt: Bloomberg Senior Editor for Technology and Strategic Industries Mike Shepard tells Bloomberg This Weekend that disappointing Big Tech earnings are intensifying investor concerns about whether massive AI spending will generate sufficient returns, as Alphabet and Intel come under particular pressure.

items.headline: Binance in Talks for Malaysia License after Five-Year Absence
items.excerpt: Binance said it’s in discussions with Malaysian regulators for a licensed business in the country, as the cryptocurrency exchange seeks a route back into a market where authorities have blocked its website and applications.

items.headline: SoftBank-Backed OPay Halts IPO to Respond to Regulatory Inquiry
items.excerpt: OPay Ltd., a Nigeria-focused payments platform, halted an initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange that was supposed to start trading on Friday, citing a regulatory inquiry.

items.headline: The Betting Coup That Rocked London’s Bookmakers Goes Unsolved
items.excerpt: Lisa Lazarus, the top cop in US horse racing, woke up one morning this summer to find a flurry of missed overseas calls and e-mails. items.headline: OpenAI’s Altman Meets Samsung Executives as Chip Crunch Deepens
items.excerpt: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman met with Samsung Group’s top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as global shortages intensify.

items.headline: OpenAI Funding Target Cut by $10 Billion as AI Slumps, FT Says
items.excerpt: OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by $10 billion as an AI stock selloff and rival Anthropic PBC’s impending public listing complicate its efforts to secure investor commitments, the Financial Times reported.

items.headline: AstraZeneca CFO on AI, Earnings, Restructuring Plan
items.excerpt: AstraZeneca Chief Financial Officer Aradhana Sarin says the drug company uses AI in almost every aspect of the work they do. She talks beating on earnings, their drug pipeline and how the company approaches dealmaking. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Meta’s Rating Outlook Cut to Negative by S&P on AI Spending
items.excerpt: S&P Global Ratings took an early step toward potentially downgrading Meta Platforms Inc.’s credit rating within the next two years, amid growing pressure on the tech company’s balance sheet stemming from elevated spending tied to artificial intelligence.

items.excerpt: Bridgewater Associates CEO Nir Bar Dea sits down with David Rubenstein for a wide-ranging conversation about the US economy, rising national debt, the dollar and explains how he sees AI reshaping the future of investing. items.excerpt: Intercontinental Exchange joined forces with one of the market operators behind offshore crypto-trading platform Hyperliquid as it seeks to bring perpetual futures products into US regulated markets. items.headline: Baseten to Raise Funding That Would Double Value to $30 Billion
items.excerpt: Artificial intelligence startup Baseten is set to raise new funding that would more than double its valuation to about $30 billion, according to people familiar with the efforts.

items.headline: Need To Rethink How AI Infrastructure Is Powered: FuelCell Energy CEO
items.excerpt: FuelCell Energy President and CEO Jason Few discusses public concerns over higher utility bills, water use and fossil-fuel infrastructure. items.headline: Opay Shares Fail to Trade After Raising $304 Million in US IPO
items.excerpt: Shares of Opay Ltd., a Nigeria-focused payments platform, didn’t begin trading in New York as expected after the company raised $304 million in a US initial public offering priced at the bottom of the range.

items.headline: Illumina CEO on Q3 Results and Business Outlook
items.excerpt: Jacob Thaysen says Illumina delivered a strong third quarter, beat expectations and raised its fourth-quarter outlook. items.headline: Power On: How Apple Is Deflecting the Duo’s Cracked Display Problem
items.excerpt: On this episode of the Power On podcast, Chris Welch joins Mark Gurman to unpack reports of cracked displays and why Apple’s limited supply has made getting a replacement so difficult. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Why Electronic Arts Shut Down BioWare And Cancelled ‘Mass Effect’
items.excerpt: Facing financial pressure, the video-game publisher chose ‘Star Wars’ over ‘Mass Effect’

items.headline: Tech Stocks Tumble as AI Fears Collide With Earnings Misses
items.excerpt: Tech stocks plunged on Friday for the second day in a row as fears around AI spending collide with disappointing earnings in big tech’s core businesses.

items.headline: Apple Overtakes Nvidia to Become World’s Most Valuable Company
items.excerpt: Apple Inc. reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company on Friday, taking the mantle from Nvidia Corp. as investors seek the perceived safety of the iPhone maker amid concerns about artificial intelligence spending.

items.headline: Intel Suffers Worst Stock Drop in Decades on Weak Forecast
items.excerpt: Intel Corp. suffered its worst stock rout in more than four decades after the PC industry slump and supply-chain snags hurt its forecast, renewing fears about the chipmaker’s turnaround bid.

items.headline: Big Tech Holds $3 Trillion in Spending Commitments for AI Boom
items.excerpt: The five largest players in the data center race have committed more than $3 trillion in spending over the coming years, pointing to massive ongoing investment in AI infrastructure.
